title.ko: 공항·호텔에서 문제 설명하기: delayed · cancelled · overbooked
title.en: solving travel problems: delayed, cancelled, overbooked

explain.ko: 여행 중 문제를 설명할 때는 현재완료(My luggage hasn't arrived)와 수동태(The flight was delayed / cancelled)를 자주 씁니다. 해결책은 Could you ...? 또는 Is it possible to ...?로 정중하게 요청합니다. 직원은 We apologise for the inconvenience(불편을 드려 죄송합니다), We'll arrange ...(~를 마련해 드리겠습니다), You are entitled to ...(~를 받으실 자격이 있습니다)로 대답합니다. 보상(compensation), 환불(refund), 대체편(alternative flight)을 구분해 두면 편리합니다.
explain.en: To explain travel problems use the present perfect (My luggage hasn't arrived) and the passive (The flight was delayed / cancelled). Ask for a solution politely with Could you ...? or Is it possible to ...? Staff answer with We apologise for the inconvenience, We'll arrange ... or You are entitled to ... Learn to separate compensation, refund and alternative flight.

head: 구조 / Structure
표현 / Phrases
예문 / Example
rows: has / have been + p.p. · hasn't arrived
Could you ...? · Is it possible to ...?

We'll arrange a hotel for you.

notes.ko: 항공편은 delayed(지연), cancelled(취소), overbooked(예약 초과)로 구분합니다.
불만을 말할 때도 정중한 어조(Could you ...?)를 유지하면 해결이 더 빠릅니다.
notes.en: Staying polite (Could you ...?) usually gets a faster solution.

notes.ko: be entitled to + 명사는 '~를 받을 권리가 있다'입니다.
notes.en: Be entitled to + noun means have the right to get something.

prompt.en: Imagine a problem at an airport or hotel and write 4 sentences explaining it and asking for a solution.

task.model: My flight was delayed by two hours, so I missed my connection. My luggage hasn't arrived either. Could you put me on the next flight? I was told you apologise for the inconvenience, but I'd like to know if I am entitled to compensation.

model_trans.ko: 제 비행기가 두 시간 지연되어서 환승편을 놓쳤어요. 제 수하물도 아직 도착하지 않았어요. 다음 비행기로 바꿔 주시겠어요? 불편을 드려 죄송하다는 말을 들었지만 보상을 받을 수 있는지 알고 싶어요.
model_trans.en: My flight was delayed by two hours, so I missed my connection. My luggage hasn't arrived either. Could you put me on the next flight? I was told you apologise for the inconvenience, but I'd like to know if I am entitled to compensation.
